# Toast

A short message that confirms an action and goes away.

**In Dense data.** Confirms a saved change. Family: feedback. Reference: Open UX (toast), MIT.

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data" title="Toast examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-toast--docs">Open Toast in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-toast--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:dense-data;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Saved, sent, exported: something people should notice without stopping.
- **Not when:** A failure people must understand (alert or dialog), or a notice that stays (alert).

Instead:

- [Alert](./alert.md): Stays on the page.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): Needs an answer.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">The words of an error</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Name the record, then the fix. Flat and specific.</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> &quot;Oops&quot; or a vague apology</div></div><div class="cap">Experts act on the message; the record and the fix are all they need. Example: “Alert ALR-2042 not saved. Threshold must be between 0 and 100.”</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A success message</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> A short confirmation with the count</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Celebration</div></div><div class="cap">Confirm and get out of the way; the next task is waiting. Example: “12 alerts exported.”</div></div></div>

## Why it works this way

Toast looks the way it does because of 4 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Toast, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How does it sound?</b><code>voice.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Terse</div><p>Experts want short labels and short messages.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>neutral</b>: A plain confirmation: Filters cleared.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: A short confirmation with the count: 12 alerts exported.</span></li><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: A background failure: name the record, then the fix.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Toast decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-tasks-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How often do people repeat actions?</b><code>tasks.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Constantly</div><p>The same actions repeat many times an hour.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>success</b>: A short confirmation with the count: 12 alerts exported.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: ghost</code> <code>Input group: inline-end</code> <code>Sidebar: default</code> <code>Alert: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>and 11 answers that follow from it: <b>Time on task</b>, <b>All day</b>, <b>Three</b>, and 8 more.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-voice-lands"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>Where do the words matter most?</b><code>voice.lands</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Errors and empty states</div><p>Errors and empty tables are where words decide the next action.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: A background failure: name the record, then the fix.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Empty: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Acting on the wrong record</div><p>Acting on the wrong row is the costly error.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Toast</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>danger</b>: A background failure: name the record, then the fix.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Button: primary</code> <code>Button: secondary</code> <code>Alert: default</code> <code>Alert: destructive</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Toast decision would reopen</small><p>and 2 answers that follow from it: <b>Status in tables</b>, <b>Errors and empty states</b>.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is announced politely without taking focus, and stays long enough to read. undefined
- [ ] Nothing people must act on lives only in a toast. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add toast
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overlay/background` | Fill of a dialog, menu or toast. | `color.surface.raised` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.raised` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.surface.raised` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.raised` → `color.slate.dark.100` |
| `overlay/radius` | Corner radius of overlays. | `radius.container` → `dense-data.theme.base.radius.container` → `radius.4` | same |
| `overlay/shadow` | Shadow of overlays. | `elevation.overlay` → `dense-data.theme.light.elevation.overlay` → `shadow.overlay` | `elevation.overlay` → `dense-data.theme.dark.elevation.overlay` → `shadow.overlay-dark` |
| `overlay/scrim` | Color that dims the page behind a dialog. | `color.surface.scrim` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.scrim` → `color.black.light.scrim` | `color.surface.scrim` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.scrim` → `color.black.dark.scrim` |
| `overlay/item-height` | Height of a menu item. | `size.control.default` → `size.32` | same |
| `tooltip/background` | Tooltip fill. | `color.surface.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.surface.inverse` → `color.slate.light.900` | `color.surface.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.surface.inverse` → `color.slate.dark.900` |
| `tooltip/label` | Tooltip text. | `color.text.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.light.color.text.inverse` → `color.slate.light.0` | `color.text.inverse` → `dense-data.theme.dark.color.text.inverse` → `color.slate.dark.50` |
